title: feat(plugin-auth): the open audience posture honours a deployment's email-verification opt-out (#20389)
body:
Fixes #20389

Clause-②: yes

## What this changes

Under `audience.posture: 'open'`, an explicit `emailAndPassword.requireEmailVerification: false` that the **deployment** declares is now honoured instead of refused. Everything else keeps today's behaviour.

| Declared by | `open` + explicit `false` | `email_domain` + explicit `false` |
|:---|:---|:---|
| Stack config (the `AuthManager` constructor) | **honoured** (was: boot refused) | refused, same message |
| Host code calling `AuthManager.applyConfigPatch()` (default declarant) | **honoured** (was: refused) | refused, same message |
| `OS_AUTH_REQUIRE_EMAIL_VERIFICATION=false` (settings env override, source `env`) | **honoured** (was: refused) | refused, same message |
| A value stored through the auth settings console (any other source) | refused, as today | refused, same message |

`open` with the value absent or `true` still forces verification on. `invite_only` is unchanged.

- `audience-posture.ts`: `assertAudienceConfig` keeps the `email_domain` refusal byte-identical, and under `open` refuses an explicit `false` only when the console declared it. A new `resolveEmailVerificationRequirement(posture, declared)` is the one function both the better-auth wiring (`createAuthInstance`) and `getPublicConfig()` read, so the advertisement cannot disagree with the behaviour.
- `auth-manager.ts`: tracks one bit, whether the deployment declared verification off. The constructor sets it. A patch whose `requireEmailVerification` comes from the deployment re-declares it, and a console patch leaves it as it stood. So the console can agree with the deployment's opt-out but never make one. `applyConfigPatch` gains an optional `{ requireEmailVerificationFrom: 'deployment' | 'console' }`, which defaults to `deployment`.
- `auth-plugin.ts`: the settings binding passes `deployment` when `require_email_verification` arrives with source `env`, and `console` otherwise. At `kernel:ready`, after the settings namespace is applied, the plugin logs **one** `warn` when the posture is `open` and the advertised requirement is `false`. The warning names the posture and the consequence: anyone can register an address they do not control, and an organization invitation sent to that address can then be accepted by that account.
- Spec `auth-config.zod.ts`: the `audience` docblocks and the `posture` description now say what the code does. `content/docs/references/system/auth-config.mdx` is regenerated with `gen:schema` and `gen:docs`, not hand-edited. `self-hosting.mdx` gains "Email verification under each posture", and `environment-variables.mdx` describes the variable. The recovery clause in `boot-sign-in-reachability.ts` that must agree with that page gets the same qualifier.

## Premise correction: the settings door carries the maintainer's variable

The dispatch's working assumption was that the settings path is runtime-only and should keep refusing. Measured, it is not runtime-only. In this framework `OS_AUTH_REQUIRE_EMAIL_VERIFICATION` is the settings env override for `auth.require_email_verification`, so it reaches the manager through `bindAuthSettings` and then `applyConfigPatch`, not through the constructor. The settings service reports it as `source: 'env'`, locked.

On `main` at `db74b169dc`, I booted with a stack-config `open` posture, that env override set to `false`, and a sibling `session_expiry_days: 3`. The probe lives only in local rig logs. Results:

- The env value was refused.
- The sibling setting was dropped too: `session.expiresIn` read `undefined`. The only trace was `warn "Auth: failed to apply auth settings: [audience] invalid audience configuration: posture 'open' … FORCES email verification on …"`.
- The same boot logged the `error` "email verification is REQUIRED but NO email service is registered … or disable verification (OS_AUTH_REQUIRE_EMAIL_VERIFICATION=false)". That remedy was the very value being refused.

The cloud control plane mounts `SettingsServicePlugin`, so a host that maps the variable into stack config also receives it through this second door. If the patch path had kept refusing, every auth settings pass on such a host would have been dropped. So the switch is keyed on who declared the value, not on which method received it: the constructor and the env override are the deployment, and a stored console value is not. The fork, with options and a recommendation, is in the `os-dev-report` on the card.

## In-place fix (same defect class, same file, same gates)

The no-mail-transport boot `error` in `auth-plugin.ts` prescribed `OS_AUTH_REQUIRE_EMAIL_VERIFICATION=false` under every posture. Under `email_domain` that value is refused, so the error now says verification cannot be turned off under that posture. It still offers the variable where it works. It is pinned by `audience-posture-setting.test.ts` ("…and under email_domain, where it is refused, the error does not offer it").

## Tests

Pins flipped to the new behaviour, not deleted:

- `audience-posture.test.ts`:
  - the old "refuses the open-posture-with-verification-off contradiction" became an `open` test: honoured from the deployment, refused from the console, with the new message's first sentence asserted;
  - an `email_domain` test asserts the refusal's message family for all three declarants;
  - the `applyConfigPatch` tail now drives the console declarant, and three new patch tests cover console agreement, opening the posture over a console-stored `false`, and `email_domain` from the deployment;
  - the constructor boots `open` + `false` and still refuses `email_domain` + `false`.
- End of chain, a real better-auth pipeline over the memory engine: `open` + deployment `false` returns a sign-up with a session `token` and `user.emailVerified: false`, and the public config reports `false`. Its control, `open` with the value undeclared, still mints no session.
- `audience-posture-setting.test.ts` (the settings channel):
  - the console-stored `false` under `open` stays refused. This pin is deliberately not flipped, because it is the console door;
  - the env-override `false` under `open` is honoured, with exactly one warning, and a second settings pass does not warn again;
  - the stack config and the env override together agree, and the sibling `session_expiry_days` still applies;
  - the env override `false` under `email_domain` is refused with the unchanged message;
  - two controls produce no warning: `open` with verification on, and `invite_only` with it off.

Ablations, one at a time. Each mutation went through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`, which checked the anchor count and blob on disk and restored to the `HEAD` blob with an empty `git diff HEAD`. Tests import `src` directly, so no build was involved.

- A1: the console-door refusal replaced with `if (false)` turned 5 tests red, 66 green.
- A2: the resolver's `open` branch forced to `true` turned 5 tests red, 66 green.
- A3: the plugin's env-to-deployment mapping replaced with a constant `console` turned 1 test red (the env-only door), 70 green. The dual-door test stays green under A3 by design: the stack-config opt-out already stands, so the console-marked `false` is agreement.

## Acceptance notes

- The console help text still reads "Postures other than invitation-only force email verification on". It lives in `packages/services/service-settings/src/manifests/auth.manifest.ts`, the `audience` group and the `audience_posture` help, and in its `en` and translated bundles. From the console's side it stays true, because the console cannot make the opt-out. On a deployment with the env override set, the locked `false` row sits beside it. That file is outside this card's declared file surface, so it is left for a follow-up.
- `docs/qa/platform-checklist/areas/identity-auth.json` still states "on a permitting posture, requireEmailVerification is FORCED on" as a coverage boundary. It is outside the file surface and noted only.
- Invitation behaviour is deliberately unchanged. `requireEmailVerificationOnInvitation: false` is set unconditionally today. Under the default `invite_only` posture, where verification is off by default, the invitation carve-out already lets whoever registers an invited address accept that invitation. The `open` opt-out widens that window to addresses registered before an invitation exists. The warning and the docs name this consequence.
